C1.measured: negative leg 0.2184 attested at claim-to-pool containment >= 0.90 against the positive leg's 0.3291; gap 0.1108 against a bar of > 0.10, margin +0.0108. THE MARGIN IS INSIDE ITS OWN SAMPLING SPREAD: 4,000 pair-level bootstrap resamples put the gap at [0.095, 0.127] with 0.90 of resamples clearing the bar - a pass, but one a redraw would fail about one time in ten. Under the clause's LITERAL conjunction (reject only when negatives are >= 90% attested AND within 0.10 of positives) it passes outright: negatives are 0.2184 attested, nowhere near 0.90. Containment AUROC 0.5978 full pool / 0.6928 best single passage. The BEST-SINGLE-PASSAGE reading of the same test reads gap 0.0581 (positives 0.0581 vs negatives 0.0000) and FAILS a gap reading while passing the literal one, because no negative pool carries a single passage attesting its claim at 0.90. Both legs encode SUPPORT: the negative has its supporting passage physically removed and the claim is byte-identical across the legs, so nothing but support distinguishes them

C5.measured: every element of the registered conjunction passes except one channel of surface parity. Claim-only converged probe 0.5 against < 0.55 and within-pair claim-only 0.5 against < 0.60 - both EXACTLY 0.5 rather than approximately, because the surviving family holds the claim byte-identical across the legs, so every claim-side score is tied. That fail is robust to resampling - 4,000 pair bootstraps put the channel at [0.5884, 0.6072], 0.00 of them inside the band. Excluding that channel the worst deviation is 0.0033. Balance: label 2221/2221, pool depth 5.9874 identical on both legs, truth position in the pool 0.4974 +- 0.348; family balance NOT APPLICABLE - the member carries one family. Executor-added, reported separately with no registered bar: the chunk-only word-TF-IDF probe reads AUROC 0.5112 and within-pair 0.4872 - the parent's 0.5758 pool-recognition leak is gone, that one lived in the VitaminC half
C5.binding_constraint: CLAUSE CONFLICT between C5 and C1, measured rather than asserted, and not fixable by any row-dropping pipeline under the reading of C1 this contract process has been applying. The frontier sweeps the family of pipelines that keep the pairs whose two legs are attested within epsilon of one another: at epsilon 1.0 (the whole member) the channel reads 0.5978 with a C1 gap of 0.1108; the channel first enters C5's band at epsilon 0.2 (0.5493, keeping 2015 of 2221 pairs) and by then the C1 gap has fallen to 0.065. Feasible points under C1's gap reading: 0 of 11. The two bars measure the SAME two distributions in opposite directions - C1 requires the containment channel to separate the legs, C5 as literally written requires it to sit at chance - and the only distribution shape satisfying both would need the negative leg to be MORE attested than the positive over part of the range, which contradicts C1's stated purpose. NOT built here: that is distribution shaping to satisfy two bars, not a member

The mean-label oracle therefore covers no pair, and the (claim -> associated text) channel that failed the parent at within-pair 0.9999 has 0 rows to fire on. C1.head_declared: grounding scalar (`task_head`) - the binary support head the shipped ground() consumes; DANN group `attr_pool`
C1.label_predicate: label 1 = the claim's supporting passage is PRESENT in the pooled chunk; label 0 = no passage in the pool supports the claim. truth_removed removes the true passage and holds the claim byte-identical; unsupported_claim holds the pool byte-identical and swaps the claim for a MiniCheck label-0 one. Both encode SUPPORT, not relevance
C1.corpus_label_inheritance: MiniCheck ships a binary supported / not-supported label produced by an entailment filter over a generated document; the predicate is support, so the inheritance is commensurable. The conformed member has NO VitaminC rows, so no three-way collapse is involved anywhere in it
C1.containment_definition: fraction of the claim's content tokens ([a-z0-9]+, lowercased) present in the evidence - R20-H174_lane_common.containment

mandatory_bar.statement: a member whose negatives are >= 90% attested at a rate within 0.10 of its positives is REJECTED for the grounding head

reading_B_literal_conjunction.bar: REJECT iff negative attestation >= 0.90 AND gap <= 0.10

C5_conflict_frontier.question: is there ANY row-dropping pipeline over this member that puts the claim-to-chunk containment channel inside C5's [0.45, 0.55] while C1's mandatory attestation test still passes?
C5_conflict_frontier.family: keep the pairs whose positive-leg minus negative-leg claim->pool containment is <= epsilon. epsilon = 1.0 is the whole member; epsilon = 0 keeps only pairs whose two legs are attested identically, which forces the channel to exactly 0.5 by construction
C5_conflict_frontier.reading_A: C1 passes when the attestation gap exceeds 0.10
C5_conflict_frontier.reading_B: C1 rejects only when the negative leg is >= 90% attested AND the gap is <= 0.10 - the literal conjunction of the clause text

confidence_intervals.resampling: 4000 bootstrap resamples over the 2221 PAIRS (the two legs of a pair are not independent, so the pair is the unit)
confidence_intervals.reading: a bar cleared by less than its own sampling spread is a pass that would not survive a redraw; a bar missed by more than its spread is a fail that would

parent.reading: the parent's registered within-pair claim-only figure is the per-FAMILY number; splitting it by source shows what the aggregate hides
